Subject: Integration discovery — SDK/auth, routing, dedicated sizing questions

Thanks again for the call earlier — good conversation. I wanted to capture a few follow-ups from our side and ask for any preliminary guidance you can share before we book a technical deep-dive next week. Attaching our internal notes.

Summary of asks from PrimeData:
- SDK + auth: we prefer an SDK-first approach; need options for API keys, short-lived tokens, and ideally mutual TLS for sensitive workloads. Any sample auth flows and bootstrap snippets would help.
- Routing & model choices: we will use embeddings + reranker for search relevance, plus a small structured-output tool-calling surface for enrichment calls. Need guidance on routing between cost/lower-latency models and higher-quality variants.
- Throughput & Dedicated sizing: expected steady-state QPS ~120 requests/sec for embedding + ranking pipeline during business hours, with 5–10% requests requiring generation (tool-calling). Peaks can hit 220 QPS for short bursts. We’d like recommended concurrency limits, queueing approaches (separate lanes?), and autoscaling guidance for Dedicated capacity.
- Structured output & tool calling: how Redwood handles tool-calling determinism and whether we should prefer structured schemas or function-calls for downstream processing.

Next steps we want from Redwood: a short post-call recap with proposed owners for tech items, a rough dedicated sizing sketch (assumptions + safety margin), and a proposed agenda for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks —
Alex
Head of ML Platforms
PrimeData Analytics

Alex — thanks for the clear list and the notes. Quick post-call recap and immediate next steps below. I've looped Grace (solutions/ops) to coordinate the Dedicated sizing and Dev (cc'd on the follow-up) will validate auth/SDK details. Attached a sizing template and draft agenda for the deep-dive.

Post-call recap (high level):
- Auth & SDK: Redwood supports API keys and short-lived JWTs; we can enable mTLS for Private/Dedicated installs. We'll share bootstraps and example SDK flows (token rotation + refresh).
- Routing: recommend policy-based routing: low-cost model for embeddings and a higher-quality variant for reranking/generation. Automatic fallback to compatible variants if capacity constrained.
- Dedicated sizing (initial sketch):
  - Steady-state target: 120 QPS (embedding + ranking), with ~10% generation.
  - Target concurrency: plan for 2 tiers: low-latency lane (tail latency SLO) and throughput lane (batching-friendly).
  - Recommended starting pool: 2 reserved inference nodes (A100-equivalent) with autoscale to 4 for burst windows; this assumes 1.5–2.0ms/token steady-state for embedding models and batching for ranking.
  - Queues: separate per-lane queues; prioritize real-time requests, allow batching in throughput lane.
- Structured output/tool-calling: recommend explicit schemas for deterministic downstream parsing; use function-calling for operations that invoke external enrichment services.

Immediate next steps:
1) Grace to draft Dedicated sizing assumptions and timeline (owner: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai).
2) Dev to validate auth options and share SDK snippets + recommended client-side retry/backoff (owner: dev.patel@redwood.ai).
3) Book a 90-minute technical deep-dive (agenda: auth & SDK, routing, queue design, throughput targets, sample load tests).

Proposed slots: Wed 10/7 10:00–11:30 PT or Thu 10/8 13:00–14:30 PT. Which works for your team?

Cheers,

> - Auth & SDK: Redwood supports API keys and short-lived JWTs; we can enable mTLS for Private/Dedicated installs. We'll share bootstraps and example SDK flows (token rotation + refresh).

Quick technical notes for the deep-dive — initial assumptions and items to validate with PrimeData:

Auth & SDK
- Supported flows: API keys (long-lived, team-scoped), ephemeral JWT via exchange endpoint (recommended for client apps), and mTLS for Private installs.
- Bootstrapping: recommend a short-lived token exchange + refresh flow in the SDK; provide code snippets for Node/Python.

Routing & Model Variants
- Policy-driven routing: implement rules based on request tags ("embedding","ranker","gen-high") and latency/cost budgets.
- Fallbacks: model variant compatibility matrix; ensure tokenizer/response shape compatibility for reranker.

Embeddings + Reranker throughput
- Embedding models are GPU-light per request but heavy in QPS; optimize by batching at the serving edge (batch windows ~10–30ms).
- Reranker: can be served in batched or streaming modes; estimate ~6–8 concurrent ranking requests per GPU core with batching.

Generation & Tool-calling
- For tool-calling: prefer structured schema for predictable parsing; function-calling is fine for dynamic ops but increases retry complexity.
- Keep tool invocations idempotent. Consider per-request annotation for routing to throughput lane vs low-latency lane.

Dedicated sizing & concurrency
- Concurrency limits: enforce per-model and per-tenant concurrency (e.g., 32 concurrent generator requests per 80GB GPU equivalent).
- Queue design: two primary queues — rt_lane (priority, small-batch, <50ms queuing target) and batch_lane (buffered, larger-batch).
- Autoscaling: scale based on queue depth + p90 latency; use predictive scale-up for expected enterprise windows.

Observability and safety margins
- Instrument per-token latency, KV cache hit rates, and per-route token cost. Recommend +30% safety margin on initial reserved pool.

I'll prepare a short snippet pack (Node/Python) and a micro-benchmark plan to validate the assumptions with PrimeData's sample payloads.

Thanks — this is very helpful and aligns with what we were expecting. A few clarifications and confirmations from PrimeData: 

Numbers / constraints
- Peak bursts: up to 250 QPS for short windows (10–15 minutes), steady-state 120 QPS.
- Latency SLO: embedding p95 < 60ms, generation p95 < 800ms for user-facing flows.
- Data retention: logs/trace for 30 days; embeddings stored for 90 days.

Security & compliance
- We will need a completed security questionnaire and SOC 2 evidence for Dedicated/Private options. We'll send our security contact's questionnaire — attaching now.

Next steps
- Confirmed: Wed 10/7 10:00–11:30 PT works for our engineering leads. Please send a calendar invite with the deep-dive agenda.
- Action: We will send representative payloads and a sample QPS profile ahead of the call so you can run the sizing template against realistic inputs.

Thanks again. Looking forward to the deep-dive.
